knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The internal duct is a separate layer. A hood scope does not include it unless the written scope names it and the person doing the work is eligible for it. Connection alone does not widen scope.
Eligibility is checked against the requirements for the specific task. Experience can be relevant evidence, but it does not confirm eligibility on its own.
A verbal instruction does not widen a written scope. Hold the task, obtain the change in writing and confirm eligibility before work starts.

practicalCriteria: Classifies five sample exhaust tasks by layer (accessible surface, ductwork, fan, fire suppression, roof or high access) and gives a scope reference for each.
Declines and refers a simulated duct request without starting the work or opening any panel, and records the referral with the person informed.
Holds a simulated verbal scope change until it is confirmed in writing and eligibility is checked, and records both steps.
passRule: All five tasks classified correctly, the duct request declined and referred with no work started, the verbal change held, and the record complete. Observed in a supervised desk exercise. A pass is not an eligibility determination and does not confer any licence, certificate or specialist authority.
evidenceRequired: Task classification sheet for the five sample tasks
Referral record for the simulated duct request
Record of the verbal change and the outcome
stopWorkCriteria: Duct, fan, fire-suppression or roof work started on the basis of a hood scope
Verbal scope change accepted without written confirmation
Access panel opened or equipment touched outside the written scope
Eligibility for a specialist task assumed from experience
